subject: Request: Early commitment release + downgrade procedure for OrbitalHealth POC
messages:
From: Sara Douglas <sara@orbitalhealth.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@orbitalhealth.com
Date: 2026-08-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOW + terms — question on early exit and downgrade

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the updated SOW. We need two clarifications before procurement can move forward: 1) Orbital wants an option to downsize after month 6 if the pilot doesn’t meet utilization targets; 2) we need an early-termination path with a predictable refund/credit approach rather than a full liability for the remainder of committed spend.

Specifically, they asked for a mechanism that allows a downgrade to a lower committed tier with 60 days notice and a pro-rated credit for unused committed capacity (not a full release). They understand there may be a one-time administrative fee.

Can Redwood approve a formal amendment that:
- Allows a single downgrade after month 6 with 60 days notice,
- Credits unused committed GPU hours at the actual usage rate less a 15% administrative deduction,
- Preserves the trial ramp schedule but allows the downgrade to be effective on the next billing cycle,
- Keeps standard confidentiality/SOC2 protections.

Procurement flagged this as a non-standard term and said they need an executive OK for any deviation from the standard ramp/termination language. Can you escalate? We’re on a tight timeline — procurement would like a response by end of day Monday.

Thanks,
Sara

--
Sara Douglas
Head of IT Procurement, OrbitalHealth
Attach: Orbital_SOW_v3.pdf
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-22T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: Early commitment release + downgrade procedure for OrbitalHealth POC

Folks — forwarding Orbital’s ask. Short version: they want a single downgrade option after month 6 with a 60-day notice and a pro-rated credit instead of strict early termination liability. Procurement requires an exec ok for any non-standard ramp/exit.

What I’m proposing (market-safe compromise):
- Allow one downgrade at month 6 with 60 days notice to the next-lower committed tier.
- Credit unused committed capacity for the remainder of the current term at the actual per-GPU-hour rate used by Orbital, minus a 20% administrative and churn adjustment (covers forecasting/sloting costs).
- One-time downgrade fee equal to 10% of remaining committed monthly charge (capped at $25k).
- Limit: applies once per 12-month term and not available during initial 30-day trial.

Pros: gets them comfortable with a POC and reduces churn risk. Cons: opens precedent — need exec sign-off and deal desk stamp.

Attachments: redwood_term_matrix.xlsx (I mapped financial impact for 3 scenarios).

Can Marissa and Laura weigh in on revenue impact, and Rishi — can you ok this approach or suggest alternate ceilings? We need to reply to procurement by Mon EOD PST.

Thanks,
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-23T08:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Early commitment release + downgrade procedure for OrbitalHealth POC

Agree with the compromise Dylan outlined with two small tweaks to reduce our downside:
1) Reduce the credit adjustment to 15% (they suggested 15% in their email and that aligns with precedent for mid-market pilots).
2) Cap the maximum credit to $200k to prevent large write-offs in case of unusually large commits.

Financial impact (quick snapshot from redwood_term_matrix.xlsx):
- Base case (expected utilization): net revenue changes are negligible.
- Downside case (20% under-utilization): short-term decrease ~ $60k; long-term retention probability increases.

Operational ask: Legal needs final language to slot into the SOW amendment. Finance to confirm we can absorb a $200k cap under the ARR model for this quarter (Laura, can you confirm).

If Finance signs off on the $200k cap and Rishi gives verbal approval to proceed with these terms, I’m comfortable offering this to Orbital with the one-time 10% downgrade fee and the 60-day notice. I’ll own customer communication and change request.

Marissa
Account Exec Lead — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-24T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Early commitment release + downgrade procedure for OrbitalHealth POC

Thanks for the brief. I’ve reviewed the proposal and the attached matrix. Decision: approve with constraints.

Executive decision (approved):
- Allow one downgrade after month 6 with 60 days notice.
- Credit unused committed capacity at actual per-GPU-hour rate less a 15% administrative deduction.
- Implement a one-time downgrade fee = max(10% of remaining monthly charge, $5k) and cap total credit exposure at $200k per contract.
- Limit this concession to pilots <= $1.5M ARR-equivalent and require Deal Desk sign-off for anything larger.
- Add a mandatory practice: Sales must log the amendment and provide a 6-month usage audit to the Customer Success team within 30 days of downgrade.

Conditions: Legal to draft precise SOW amendment language that preserves our standard indemnities and SLA. Finance (Laura) to confirm accounting treatment; if the estimated exposure exceeds $200k we revert to standard early-termination liability.

Marissa — proceed to offer these terms to Orbital. Laura — please confirm accounting by EOD tomorrow.

Rishi
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
